item.title: Researcher demonstrates data exfiltration from Claude AI assistant using web browsing capabilities to leak personal information [ ! ] [ ⬢ ]
item.description: A researcher explored security vulnerabilities in the Claude AI assistant's memory system and demonstrated how it could be tricked into leaking sensitive personal information such as full name, employer, and security question answers. The experiment exploited Claude's web browsing tools, particularly the web_fetch feature, to navigate a controlled website and exfiltrate data through URL requests without detection. The researcher found that Claude's memory system stores detailed user profiles, which could be used maliciously if accessed improperly. Although Anthropic implemented safeguards restricting web_fetch to specific URL criteria, the researcher bypassed these by creating a navigable web directory that Claude could follow autonomously. This approach allowed the extraction of private data despite the AI's sandboxing and security measures. The findings highlight potential risks in AI assistants that accumulate extensive personal data and use web browsing tools, emphasizing the need for stronger security controls to prevent unauthorized data leakage or exploitation.

item.title: Bonsai releases 27B-class language model variants that run on phones and laptops using low-bit weight compression [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
item.description: Bonsai announced Bonsai 27B, a 27-billion-parameter multimodal language model based on Qwen3.6 27B, which is the first of its size to run on a phone. The model comes in two compressed variants: a 5.9 GB ternary-weight version for laptops and a 3.9 GB 1-bit-weight version that fits on an iPhone 17 Pro, enabling complex reasoning, tool use, and vision tasks locally without cloud dependency. Both variants maintain high accuracy, retaining 90-95% of full-precision performance across benchmarks including math, coding, and tool calling.

item.title: Mindgard reports unpatched Cursor IDE vulnerability allowing automatic execution of malicious git.exe in project roots, persisting over six months despite multiple disclosures [ ! ] [ ⬢ ]
item.description: Mindgard disclosed a critical vulnerability in the Cursor AI-assisted development environment that allows arbitrary code execution when opening a project containing a malicious git.exe in the repository root on Windows. This issue requires no user interaction and has remained unpatched for over six months despite repeated reports and engagement attempts with Cursor's security team. Cursor, used by millions of developers and thousands of companies, continues to ship new versions without addressing the flaw. The vulnerability was first reported in December 2025 and confirmed by HackerOne, but Cursor's response has been minimal, with the bug bounty report initially closed as out of scope and subsequent follow-ups ignored. Mindgard recommends temporary mitigations such as using AppLocker policies on managed Windows systems or opening untrusted repositories in isolated environments until a fix is released. The case raises concerns about Cursor's security processes and transparency with affected users.

item.title: Developer releases script to replace repetitive phrases like 'load-bearing' in Claude AI responses using a MessageDisplay hook [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A developer shared a method to customize Claude AI's output by replacing overused phrases such as "load-bearing" and "honest takes" with alternative words using a MessageDisplay hook script. The script performs text substitutions on Claude's responses, allowing users to tailor the AI's vocabulary to reduce frustration or add humor. The solution involves creating a Python script with predefined phrase replacements, placing it in the Claude hooks directory, and configuring the settings file to activate the hook at startup. This approach enables users to modify Claude's language dynamically without altering the AI model itself.

item.title: LeMario: Training a JEPA World Model on Super Mario Bros to predict game dynamics and plan reward-free actions [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: LeMario is a project that implements a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) trained on Super Mario Bros gameplay frames and actions to learn world dynamics without rewards. The model encodes game frames and actions into latent representations and uses a transformer-based predictor with adaptive normalization to forecast future states, aiming to enable reward-free planning in the game. The model was trained on over 700,000 frames from 280 episodes across 32 levels and demonstrated the ability to generalize to unseen episodes and predict several steps ahead better than baselines. However, while it could move Mario toward nearby image goals, it struggled with longer-range planning and navigating major obstacles, indicating it learned to predict game states but not necessarily how to progress through the levels. The project includes a detailed technical walkthrough and analysis of the model's architecture, training process, and limitations.

item.title: OpenAI employees donate over $215,000 to Guardrails Alliance super PAC opposing AI industry group led by OpenAI president Greg Brockman [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Several current and former OpenAI employees have contributed more than $215,000 to Guardrails Alliance, a super PAC advocating for stricter AI regulations and opposing Leading the Future, a pro-AI industry group supported by OpenAI president Greg Brockman. Guardrails Alliance launched with $5 million in funding and aims to raise $15 million this election cycle to counterbalance the $100 million backing Leading the Future has received from tech leaders. The donations from OpenAI staff highlight internal tensions over the company's political influence and AI policy direction, as some employees express concern about Brockman's involvement with Leading the Future. OpenAI has stated that Brockman's political activities are personal and not representative of the company, while employees are free to engage politically on their own. Guardrails Alliance cofounder Shaunna Thomas emphasized that their strategy relies on public opinion rather than matching the opposition's financial resources dollar-for-dollar.

item.title: ASML raises 2026 sales forecast to €43-45 billion after Q2 beats guidance with €9.3 billion revenue, citing strong AI-driven chip demand [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: ASML reported Q2 2026 net sales of €9.3 billion and net income of €2.9 billion, exceeding its guidance and prompting the company to raise its full-year sales forecast to €43-45 billion from €36-40 billion. CEO Christophe Fouquet attributed the strong first-half order intake to AI-related investments driving demand for advanced logic and memory chips, leading ASML to plan a 30% increase in EUV system capacity for 2027 and consider further expansion in 2028. China accounted for roughly 20% of ASML's sales despite the MATCH Act restrictions on DUV exports, with demand focused on logic chips for domestic customers. The company noted that the legislation has not yet impacted its order book, but the compliance window closing in late September could affect future sales. ASML's outlook aligns with strong performance from key customers like TSMC and SK Hynix, indicating sustained growth across the AI chip supply chain.

item.title: Weco.ai demonstrates recursive self-improvement with AIDE2, an AI system that autonomously improved its own research algorithm within eight days [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Weco.ai has developed AIDE2, an AI system that provides the first experimental evidence of recursive self-improvement by autonomously enhancing its own autoresearch capabilities. Over eight days, AIDE2 iteratively optimized its inner research loop, producing seven improved versions that outperformed a manually tuned agent refined over two years. AIDE2 operates with two nested autoresearch loops: an inner loop optimizing code against evaluations and an outer loop optimizing the inner loop's harness code. The system reduced prompt size by 16 times, created a novel search algorithm, and developed defenses against reward hacking, significantly lowering cheating rates in benchmark tests. This achievement marks Level 1 recursive self-improvement, where the system improves itself more efficiently than human researchers under a fixed compute budget.

Research Vice President Steve Kleynhans forecasts that local AI models will handle tasks like speech, chat, and image generation, complementing cloud services and transforming PCs into key AI infrastructure components. He expects AI PC power to increase tenfold by 2031 and advises organizations to consider AI PCs in their IT infrastructure planning, especially as third-generation AI PCs emerge in 2027.

item.title: Analysis finds Markdown best for AI working documents, AsciiDoc for human-reviewed AI specs, and HTML for publishing in AI specification projects [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A project with over 600 documents including AI specifications evaluated Markdown, AsciiDoc, and HTML formats to determine the most effective for AI-related documentation. The study found Markdown suitable for disposable AI-generated content, AsciiDoc for curated human-reviewed specifications, and HTML primarily as a publishing format due to its higher markup overhead and lower readability. The evaluation considered file size, readability, usability in tools like GitHub and IntelliJ, and the ability to embed HTML when needed without cluttering the source. The conclusion emphasizes choosing formats that balance human reviewability, tool compatibility, and efficient AI consumption rather than just minimizing token count.

The strategy reflects Australia's broader approach to technological change, drawing on its history of pioneering social reforms and setting global standards. Officials highlight the importance of shaping AI development responsibly to seize opportunities and manage risks, with efforts to attract frontier AI investment and foster ethical use across industries.

item.title: AITerm launches a native macOS terminal with AI command proposals, error fixes, and a safety gate for secure command execution [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: AITerm is a new native macOS terminal application that integrates an AI command loop allowing users to describe tasks in plain English, receive editable command suggestions, and approve before execution. It includes features like error diagnosis, multi-step task automation, and a safety gate that classifies command risk levels to prevent unsafe operations. The terminal supports local AI models such as Ollama and cloud APIs including OpenAI, Anthropic, and Claude, ensuring privacy by running requests locally or directly with providers without intermediaries. Users can manage multiple tabs and splits, save workspaces, and create runbooks to automate sequences with pre-flight approvals. The safety gate enforces risk assessments on commands, blocking destructive or sensitive actions unless explicitly approved, even in autopilot mode.

The service includes features like intelligent routing for fast, reliable responses, a library of prompt templates for various tasks including coding, design, and security, and the ability to export and share code sessions. UltraWork targets indie hackers, agencies, and small teams seeking a frictionless AI coding companion with human customer support and no setup fees or contracts.

item.title: Decibri launches a unified audio layer for AI agents and Voice AI applications with real-time microphone capture, playback, and voice activity detection across Python, Node.js, and Rust [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Decibri has introduced a cross-platform audio infrastructure designed for real-time voice applications, enabling developers to capture microphone audio, play sound through speakers, and stream audio data with zero system dependencies or setup. The platform supports Python, Node.js, and Rust with pre-built binaries, offering features like configurable sample rates, voice activity detection using a bundled Silero VAD model, and native streaming interfaces for seamless integration with voice agents and WebSocket pipelines. The solution emphasizes low-latency, predictable audio I/O without requiring system audio libraries or build tools, making it suitable for server-side voice agent backends, CLI tools, and edge development. Decibri also provides utilities for recording audio to disk and supports browser environments through its Node.js package, aiming to simplify real-time audio handling across multiple platforms including Windows, macOS, and Linux.

item.title: Echoo.ai launches tool enabling developers to write code in native languages with automated English shipping to improve speed and collaboration [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Echoo.ai introduces a software development approach that allows developers to write code in their native languages while the system automatically handles translation and deployment in English. This method aims to reduce the cognitive load and time costs associated with writing in a second language, improving accessibility and productivity for diverse teams. Research shows that non-native English speakers spend significantly more time reading and writing in English due to cognitive translation costs. Echoo.ai's solution separates idea generation from language conversion, leveraging AI to automate the English pass and cut writing time by over 50%, narrowing productivity gaps between native and non-native speakers. By automating the translation step, this approach helps developers focus on their ideas without the mental overhead of language switching, potentially reshaping collaboration in global software development and accelerating workflows across multilingual teams.

item.title: Hassabis' AI Standards Idea Gets Support-What's Next? [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]

Hassabis' idea is that this new group could review frontier AI models to ensure they don't pose a danger in areas such as cybersecurity and biological threats or in any other way (more here). item.title: Prepare for Customer Calls with Google Gemini [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Pitching a new customer for the first time can be intimidating. Especially if most of your conversations are with existing clients and warm leads, it is often difficult to know where to start with a new customer. The prospect may know little to nothing about your product or service offering, and it is easy to fall into the trap of over-explaining, racing through as much information as possible out of fear of leaving something out. Gemini can help you get beyond the blank page and the blinking cursor. By providing Gemini with specific information about your product and the prospect's needs, you can generate first drafts of custom call scripts and elevator pitches in record time-and then go back and forth in a natural-language chat until you feel fully prepared for your pitch meeting. Step 1: Generate a Custom Script Don't let perfectionism keep you from getting started. Instead, quickly gather the information that is relevant to your upcoming call and upload it to Gemini. This might include product one-pagers, offer sheets, pricing pages, and any input forms or other information that the prospect has already provided. More is usually better, but Gemini can get started with whatever you have at your fingertips. Next, type a prompt asking Gemini to draft a call script. Your prompt doesn't need to be more than a few sentences, but it should be as detailed as possible to make sure Gemini understands what you're looking for. Here's an example: Draft a customized script for me to follow during my sales call with a prospect. The call will happen over a video call and is set to last 30 minutes. Make sure to add the following in the script: how [company products/solutions] can help address potential customer's pain points, how [company]'s delivery system guarantees seamless and timely delivery, competitive pricing and volume-discount table, and space for a customer reference in the [customer's industry] industry. Step 2: Refine Your Pitch Remember that Gemini's response is a starting point, not a finished product. You may find that your own thinking becomes sharper the moment you have a draft that you can react to. When Gemini produces an insightful angle or clever transition, these might spark your imagination, inspiring you to build on what's already there. Or, if a section feels out-of-place or doesn't align with your own voice, you may find yourself pushing back with better ideas. Either way, having a "thought partner" can be invaluable as you revise the initial draft into a polished pitch. If you still feel stuck, you can simply respond to Gemini's questions in the chat. For instance, Gemini may ask for specific details that will help tailor the script, such as the job role or main priority of the person you'll be speaking with. Step 3: Boil It Down Your script outline gives you a roadmap for your entire meeting, but you may also want a high-impact hook for times when you only have 30 seconds to communicate your company's value proposition, rather than 30 minutes. Try this prompt: Generate an elevator pitch for [product name] and include key benefits, competitive points of differentiation, and the pain points that [product name] solves for. Because you are working within the same chat thread, Gemini already has all the relevant details about your product and your prospect, which it can now distill into a quick, sharpened pitch. Here again, you can continue to go back and forth until you feel the messaging is exactly right. Step 4: Finalize Your Meeting Prep Before you jump onto your video call, take a few minutes to review your script one last time. The pre-meeting pressure will likely heighten your focus, causing you to catch potential missteps that you missed earlier. Bring your own judgment and expertise to this final review, taking care to ensure that the script is both human and grounded in the reality of your offer and the prospect's needs. Gemini can help you turn your marketing materials into tailored pitches, and your own expertise can help turn these pitches into deals.

item.title: Evaluating Models is Getting Even Harder [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: As AI gets more advanced, researchers are increasingly telling me that it's also getting harder to evaluate how good AI actually is at various tasks. Most obviously, as AI improves, it quickly saturates all the benchmarks we have today and researchers have to rush to come up with even harder evaluations that the models won't immediately ace. There are more subtle reasons as well. Researchers at the International Conference on Machine Learning said last week that today's models have gotten so good, they can work on a task for hours or days. That's great, but it also means evaluating their performance can take hours or days as well. We're quickly approaching a point where models can "work for weeks or indefinitely," OpenAI researcher Noam Brown said during an ICML panel last week. (You can imagine that a model would want to work for that long in cases like drug discovery, where a model might spend weeks running experiments and analyzing the results of those experiments.) That means evaluating a model could eventually take longer than training that model in the first place, Brown said. Not only is that difficult to do practically, but it could also slow down the process of model development.

item.title: Americans Deserve a Dividend From AI Companies' Riches [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Suddenly everyone wants to hand the government a piece of AI. Sam Altman has discussed giving up a stake in OpenAI. Washington already owns 10% of Intel and has said it will take a cut of Nvidia's China chip revenue. Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.) wants every major AI lab to put half of its stock into a new sovereign wealth fund. In soccer terms, these are shots on goal, but nobody is scoring. Every one of these proposals ends in the same place: equity parked with the government. The Treasury gets richer, or a fund gets set up. Not one of them says what happens to an actual citizen-how a person earns a stake, holds it or ever sees a dollar from it. This is a big problem that the tech giants haven't solved. Luckily, big ideas can come from small towns, so let me take you to one.

item.title: Google and Industry Partners Announce Agentic Resource Discovery Specification for AI Agents [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
item.description: Google and industry partners announced Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD) Specification, an open standard for publishing, discovering, and verifying AI tools, APIs, and agents. ARD introduces a discovery layer built on catalogs and registries, enabling dynamic capability discovery while leveraging existing protocols such as MCP and OpenAPI for execution and emphasizing trust and interoperability. By Leela Kumili

item.title: Article: Comprehension at AI Speed: Building a Context Store for Evolutionary Architecture [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: AI makes the first 80% of development feel fast, but hides architectural complexity until it's too late. To prevent system instability, engineering leaders must shift from raw throughput to systemic comprehension. By unifying spec-anchored SDD, TDD, and automated fitness functions into a repo-bound "Context Store," teams can ensure AI agents and human reviewers evolve code safely. By Stella Berhe, Stephan Bragner, Vikram Maran, Anand Jayaraman
